# TideSurf

> Stateful Chromium tools for agents. TideSurf compresses the live DOM into compact text and assigns action IDs to current elements.

Package: @tidesurf/core
CLI: tidesurf
Runtime: Node.js 18+ or Bun 1+
Docs: https://tidesurf.org/docs
Source: https://github.com/TideSurf/core

## Install

```sh
brew install TideSurf/tap/tidesurf
# or
npm install --global @tidesurf/core
```

## Use as your agent tool

TideSurf installs into an agent in three ways, from lightest to deepest:

1. MCP server: add `tidesurf mcp` to any MCP client config (see the MCP section).
2. Agent Skills: the npm package ships `skills/tidesurf-browser`, an Agent Skills document that teaches the agent the TideSurf workflow. Install it with `npx skills add TideSurf/core`, or copy `skills/tidesurf-browser` into your project's `.agents/skills/` directory.
3. Agent Plugin: the package root is a valid Agent Plugins v1.0.0 directory (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/`). Point any compatible client (VS Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Kiro) at a checkout or the unpacked npm package to register both the MCP server and the skill.

TideSurf is also a host: it loads Agent Plugins from `.tidesurf/plugins/` (project) and `~/.tidesurf/plugins/` (user), and Agent Skills from `.agents/skills/`, `.tidesurf/skills/`, and the same paths under `~`. Plugin skills and MCP servers become available to the agent through the `list_skills`/`read_skill` tools, the `skills`/`plugins` CLI commands, and the MCP adapter (plugin MCP servers are proxied into `tidesurf mcp` under `<plugin>__<tool>` names). Set `TIDESURF_PLUGINS_DIR`/`TIDESURF_SKILLS_DIR` to replace the default roots, and `TIDESURF_EXTENSIONS=all|user|off` to control scope: the default `user` loads only your own extensions, while project-scoped (repository-shipped) extensions require the explicit `all` opt-in.

## Agent CLI

The first tool command starts a private local daemon and a managed headless browser. Separate CLI invocations reuse the same browser, active tab, open tabs, and element ID maps. The default session name is `default`.

```sh
tidesurf navigate https://example.com
tidesurf get_state
tidesurf click B1
tidesurf stop
```

Use `--session <name>` on every command for an independent workflow:

```sh
tidesurf --session docs navigate https://example.com/docs
tidesurf --session docs get_state --max-tokens 800
```

Session commands:

- `start`: start the session daemon and browser
- `status`: report session and browser state without starting either
- `stop`: stop the named session; repeated calls succeed, and a recorded daemon whose socket vanished is terminated
- `tools`: list the shared tool registry
- `help [command]`: show generated help
- `call <tool> --input <json|->`: call an exact tool identifier with JSON; `-` reads stdin
- `inspect <url>`: one-shot compatibility command
- `mcp`: run the MCP stdio adapter
- `skills [name]`: list discovered Agent Skills, or print one skill's document
- `plugins`: list discovered Agent Plugins with diagnostics

Direct tool commands, in registry order:

1. `get_state`
2. `navigate`
3. `click`
4. `type`
5. `select`
6. `scroll`
7. `extract`
8. `evaluate`
9. `list_tabs`
10. `new_tab`
11. `switch_tab`
12. `close_tab`
13. `search`
14. `screenshot`
15. `upload`
16. `clipboard_read`
17. `clipboard_write`
18. `download`
19. `list_skills`
20. `read_skill`

Use `tidesurf help <command>` for exact positionals and flags. Page-state flags:

- `get_state --max-tokens <n> --mode <full|minimal|interactive>`
- `get_state --full-page` disables normal viewport filtering
- `get_state --include-hidden` includes hidden nodes and disables viewport filtering
- `screenshot --element-id <id> | --full-page`
- `screenshot --output <file>` writes a selected file
- `screenshot --output -` writes raw PNG bytes to stdout

Without `--output`, screenshot writes a unique temporary PNG and prints its absolute path.

Element and full-page captures, plus SDK `defaultViewport` values, are limited to 16,384 px per side and 12,000,000 total pixels.

Default output is readable text or pretty JSON. `--json` returns the ToolResult shape:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": "..." }
```

Exit codes: 0 Success; 2 CLI usage or input parsing error; 3 Session or browser startup/connection error; 4 Tool execution failed; 5 Daemon authentication, transport, or protocol error.

## Browser startup

Managed isolated Chromium is the default. Launch is headless unless `--headful` is set. TideSurf selects an ephemeral debugging port unless `--port` is explicit.

Browser resolution order:

1. `--chrome-path`
2. `CHROME_PATH`
3. executable on `PATH`
4. platform install locations, including macOS user applications and Windows LOCALAPPDATA

Channel order: stable, Beta, Dev, Canary, Chromium. Select one with `--channel stable|beta|dev|canary|chromium`. Edge and Brave need `--chrome-path`. TideSurf never downloads a browser.

Without an explicit endpoint, `--auto-connect` tries a current Chrome profile DevToolsActivePort entry, then a conventional local CDP endpoint, before local launch; `--connect-only` runs the same checks and never launches. An explicit `--browser-url` or `--host`/`--port` endpoint never falls back to a different running browser: `--connect-only` fails when it does not answer, and `--auto-connect` launches fresh for a local endpoint or fails for a remote one.

Startup and policy flags:

`--headful`, `--auto-connect`, `--connect-only`, `--browser-url`, `--host`, `--port`, `--chrome-path`, `--channel`, `--user-data-dir`, `--read-only`, `--allow-localhost`, `--allow-private-hosts`, repeatable `--file-access-root`, `--timeout`.

For `download`, `--timeout` after the command sets the file wait, which defaults to 30,000 ms independent of the session timeout. Put the global `--timeout` before `download` to set the session operation timeout.

Timer-backed SDK and tool timeouts are positive whole milliseconds up to 2,147,483,647. CLI aggregate request budgets must stay at or below 1,073,741,823 ms.

Session policy is immutable. Later calls may omit startup flags or repeat matching standalone values. Browser-mode flag combinations must resolve to the stored mode, and a repeated `--file-access-root` set must match the complete stored list. Conflicting explicit values require `stop` or another session name. Sessions have no idle shutdown.

## Page format

```text
# Example Search
> example.com/search | 0/1200 800vh

NAV
  [L1](/) Home
FORM F1
  I1 ~Search... ="TideSurf"
  [B1] Search
```

Prefixes: L link, B button, I input, S select, F form, T table, D dialog.

IDs refer to the in-memory state map. Read new state after navigation or a dynamic page update. Never guess a replacement ID after a stale-ID error.

Default state uses viewport filtering. `includeHidden: true` is a full-DOM debugging override, not only a CSS-hidden override.

## SDK

```ts
import { TideSurf } from "@tidesurf/core";

const browser = await TideSurf.launch();
await browser.navigate("https://example.com");
const state = await browser.readPage({ maxTokens: 1000 });
await browser.getPage().click("B1");
await browser.close();
```

`TideSurf.launch(options)` strictly launches and owns Chrome. An unspecified launch port is ephemeral. `TideSurf.connect(options)` strictly attaches and defaults to `localhost:9222`. Closing an attached instance only disconnects.

`TideSurfOptions.channel` accepts `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary`, or `chromium`.

The package-level `getToolDefinitions()` and a normal instance return all 20 schemas used by the CLI and MCP. A read-only instance or `getToolDefinitions({ readOnly: true })` returns the eight observation schemas. `getToolExecutor()` accepts `{ name, input }` and returns ToolResult.

## Read-only mode

Allowed tools: `get_state`, `extract`, `list_tabs`, `switch_tab`, `search`, `screenshot`, `list_skills`, `read_skill`.

Blocked operations: navigation, interaction, evaluation, clipboard, upload/download, tab creation, tab closure. Enforcement applies in the registry, executor, MCP adapter, TideSurf methods, and SurfingPage returned by `getPage()`.

## Evaluate

`evaluate` runs arbitrary JavaScript in the page. TideSurf validates input shape and size; it does not provide a JavaScript sandbox. CDP values such as `NaN`, infinity, negative zero, and bigint return as JSON-safe strings. Read-only mode removes and rejects the tool.

## Files and URLs

SDK uploads and downloads stay inside `fileAccessRoots`. Omit the option for the working directory and OS temporary directory; pass `fileAccessRoots: []` to disable SDK filesystem operations. The CLI adds roots with repeatable `--file-access-root` flags.

One download may run through a `SurfingPage` connection at a time. TideSurf checks the destination again after directory creation and before enabling browser downloads.

Localhost, loopback, private, and link-local navigation is blocked by default. Use `allowLocalhost` or `allowPrivateHosts` only for trusted targets.

## MCP

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tidesurf": {
      "command": "tidesurf",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP adapter registers the shared 20 tools and the `launch_browser` lifecycle tool. Tool calls may omit the `arguments` object. Screenshot results become image blocks. Failed tool calls set `isError`. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` are optional package dependencies. When Agent Plugins with MCP servers are installed, the adapter connects to them and proxies their tools as `<plugin>__<tool>`; plugin failures are isolated per server and logged to stderr.
